lines.trans: How are your preparations for studying abroad going?
Right before Director Muranishi was arrested, I spoke with him by phone.
He happily told me he had made a masterpiece and wanted to show it to me.
A man named Ikezawa scouted me, but I don't think he and I will ever understand each other.
Are you planning to leave the director locked up like this forever?

words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

lines.trans: Rescuing the director takes huge money. I cannot raise it on my own.
Can't you sell my film? I cannot just sit still and do nothing.

words.gram: Past た-form of する (to do/happen).

lines.trans: I will handle my mother myself. My resolve is already set!
Still, to get stores to carry it, we must prove it will definitely be a hit.
Then I will step out in public and promote the film myself.
That will drag your family's lives into it too, you know?
Together with Director Muranishi, we can change public perceptions too.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

examples.text: 最高傑作ができたから私に見せたいって、うれしそうに言ってたんです。
examples.trans: He happily told me he had made a masterpiece and wanted to show it to me.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Used as a noun or adverbially to mean 'for life / forever'.

examples.trans: I will never forget it for the rest of my life.

examples.text: これは一生の思い出です。
池沢という方にスカウトされていたんですが、一生分かり合えないと思います。
examples.trans: A man named Ikezawa scouted me, but I don't think he and I will ever understand each other.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in state

meanings.note: After a te-form (積んでおきました, contracted 入っとけ), indicates doing something in advance or staying put.

examples.text: 窓を開けておきました。
ここに置いておきます。
examples.trans: I will leave it here for now.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 助けたい人間も救えるんじゃないか？
examples.trans: And couldn't you also rescue the person you want to save?

examples.text: 監督を救うには大金が必要なんだ。俺だけじゃ集めらんない。
examples.trans: Rescuing the director takes huge money. I cannot raise it on my own.

examples.text: 監督を救うには大金が必要なんだ。俺だけじゃ集めらんない。
examples.trans: Rescuing the director takes huge money. I cannot raise it on my own.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

examples.text: 監督を救うには大金が必要なんだ。俺だけじゃ集めらんない。
examples.trans: Rescuing the director takes huge money. I cannot raise it on my own.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Mental readiness to face something difficult or risky.

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Adverb emphasizing that there is nothing more.

examples.text: ただ本当のことを言っただけです。
ただ静かに待っていた。
ただ販売するには、必ずヒットするってことを示さないと。
examples.trans: Still, to get stores to carry it, we must prove it will definitely be a hit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
ただ販売するには、必ずヒットするってことを示さないと。
examples.trans: Still, to get stores to carry it, we must prove it will definitely be a hit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.
Opposite of 裏 (hidden side); also means 'outside/front'.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.
Go outside / come into the open.

examples.text: だったら私が表に出て宣伝活動をします、自分で。
examples.trans: Then I will step out in public and promote the film myself.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Standard word for family.

examples.text: 週末は家族と過ごします。
examples.trans: I spend weekends with my family.
Everyone in my family is doing well.

meanings.note: Refers to a person's life, career, and experiences.

examples.text: 人生を諦めないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't give up on life.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: 村西監督と一緒ならイメージだって変えられます。
examples.trans: Together with Director Muranishi, we can change public perceptions too.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle adding emphasis, similar to でも or も.

examples.text: 俺だって言いたいことがある。
examples.trans: I have something I want to say too.

examples.text: 誰だって間違いはある。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
